# `Q-12-6` — `listing: false` Not Allowed

> `listing: false` is not allowed; remove the key entirely
> instead.

## What this means

To turn a page into a listing, set the `listing:` key in its
front matter to a non-`false` value. To *not* have a listing on
a page, omit the key. Quarto does not treat `listing: false` as
"turn listings off on this page" — there is nothing to turn off
when the key is absent.

The parser emits this warning rather than silently treating
`listing: false` as the absence of the key, because both
interpretations are plausible and the user should pick.

## Why this happens

Most often the author is trying to override a setting from a
parent `_metadata.yml` or `_quarto.yml` that turns on a listing
project-wide. Setting `listing: false` looks like a natural
override but is not the supported way to opt out.

## How to fix

To opt out of a project-wide listing on a single page, instead
of `listing: false`, override the relevant project-level setting
in a different way — for example, by changing the project's
listing scope or by moving the page out of the listing directory.

If the goal was simply "don't make this page a listing," delete
the `listing:` line from the front matter.
